preparedWork.draft:
Title tag (proposed): How to make images smaller on a Mac | Macloving
Meta description (proposed): Shrink Mac images for sharing or the web, and choose what happens to your originals and photo details. Built-in Preview steps, plus Diet Image.

How to make images smaller on your Mac

Large image files fill your disk and are slow to email or upload. Before you shrink anything, decide two things: what happens to your originals, and what photo details (such as location) travel with each image.

Option 1: Preview (built in)
Apple documents resizing several images together in Preview. Work on copies so originals stay untouched.
1. Open the images in one Preview window.
2. Select them in the sidebar.
3. Choose Tools, then Adjust Size.
4. To reduce file size, select Resample image and lower the resolution. The estimated size appears below.
5. To lower quality instead, choose File, then Export, pick JPEG and move the Quality slider. Save under a new name.

Option 2: Diet Image
Diet Image is a Macloving app in the Photo & Video category. Its page describes it as an image optimizer. It tries several optimizers on each image and keeps a new version only when it is valid and actually smaller.
1. Check you are on macOS 26.0 or later.
2. Choose what happens to originals: replace with recovery, save beside the original, or export to a folder. By default the recovery store keeps originals for 7 days, up to 2 GB in total; both limits can be changed in Settings.
3. Choose which photo details to keep or remove: location, camera details, comments and copyright are set separately.
4. Pick a preset. Lossless leaves pixels alone, Balanced trims gently, and Smallest compresses hard.
5. Drop images or whole folders on the window or the Dock icon.
6. Review the results. Every output is decoded and checked before it is accepted, and the inspector offers split, before, after and difference views.

Which should you use?
If Preview does what you need, keep using it. Diet Image is worth a look if you want to fit a size limit in KB or MB, work across several formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF, JPEG XL), or control originals and photo details in one place.

Good to know
Balanced is lossy, so pixels do change, though results must pass a strict similarity check. Smallest allows more loss. Lossless skips AVIF and HEIC. Diet Image asks for no special permissions, optimizes images on your Mac without uploading them, and only contacts macloving.app to check for updates, which you can turn off in Settings.

About Macloving
Every Macloving app is included in one membership for $2 a month or $20 a year, with no free trial, and some apps are free for everyone.

See the Diet Image app page: https://macloving.app/apps/dietimage

drafts.title: Draft: Guide copy for Diet Image (title chosen)
drafts.body:
Title tag (chosen): How to Reduce Image File Size on Mac (Preview and Diet Image) | Macloving
Meta description (chosen): Make Mac images smaller for sharing or uploading. Use built-in Preview for one-off jobs, or Diet Image to batch and control originals and photo details.

H1: How to reduce image file size on a Mac

Large images are slow to send and fill your disk. There are two main levers: reduce the pixel dimensions, or compress the file more. Before you start, decide what happens to your originals.

Option 1: Preview (built in)
Resizing changes the file, so work on a copy if you still need the original.
1. In Finder, select the image, right-click and choose Open With, then Preview.
2. Choose Tools, then Adjust Size.
3. Tick Resample image and lower the Resolution or dimensions. The new size is shown in the dialog.
4. Save the result under a new name.
For several images at once, open them in the same Preview window, select them in the sidebar, then use Tools, Adjust Size.
To lower quality instead of size, choose File, then Export, pick JPEG and move the Quality slider. Menu names can differ between macOS versions.
A note on formats: PNG files are usually larger than JPEG, so converting a photo from PNG to JPEG can shrink it a lot.

Option 2: Diet Image
Diet Image is a Macloving image optimizer for Mac. Drop images or whole folders on its window or Dock icon. It tries several optimizers on each image and keeps a new version only when it is valid and actually smaller.
1. Check you are on macOS 26.0 or later.
2. Choose what happens to originals: replace with recovery, save beside the original, or export to a folder. By default, originals kept for recovery are held for 7 days, up to 2 GB in total; you can change both limits in Settings.
3. Choose which photo details to keep or remove. Location, camera details, comments and copyright are set separately.
4. Pick a preset: Lossless leaves pixels alone, Balanced trims gently, Smallest compresses hard.
5. Optionally fit a limit in KB or MB, or convert to JPG, PNG, WebP or JPEG XL.
6. Compare results in the inspector's split, before, after and difference views.

Which should you use?
For a single picture, Preview is usually enough. Diet Image is worth a look for batches, size limits, nine formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF and JPEG XL, with animated GIF and WebP staying animated), or control over originals and photo details.

Good to know
Balanced is lossy, so pixels do change, though results must pass a strict similarity check. Smallest allows more loss and visible changes are possible. Lossless skips AVIF and HEIC. Your images are optimized on your Mac and never uploaded; the app only checks macloving.app for updates, which you can turn off in Settings.

About Macloving
Every Macloving app is included in one membership for $2 a month or $20 a year, with no free trial, and some apps are free for everyone.

See the Diet Image app page: https://macloving.app/apps/dietimage

drafts.title: Draft: Search wording decision and test log
drafts.body:
TITLE DECISION
Chosen: 'How to Reduce Image File Size on Mac'. Reasons from public results read: Trend Micro's page is titled 'How to Resize or Reduce Image Size on Mac', Setapp's 'How to reduce image file size on Mac, iPhone & iPad easily', and iDownloadBlog's and Watermarkly's use 'compress images on Mac'. 'Reduce file size' matches the real goal (smaller files, not just smaller dimensions) and appears in the top titles. 'Compress an image on Mac' is a close variant and is covered in the meta description. Treat the query as a hypothesis: search volume and competition are unknown, and no private Search Console data exists yet. The title does not depend on measuring them.
Competition note: the pages read do not mention Diet Image or Macloving, so the guide's edge is the Diet Image comparison and the originals/photo-details controls.

TEST LOG (work on a COPY of a mixed folder: PNG screenshot, JPEG with location data, HEIC, animated GIF, WebP, large TIFF; note file sizes in Finder first)
A. Diet Image
1. Welcome guide lets you choose originals handling and photo details?
2. Replace with recovery: output replaces source, original recoverable; Settings default 7 days and 2 GB?
3. Save beside the original: new file next to source, source untouched?
4. Export to a folder: output lands in the chosen folder?
5. Lossless, Balanced, Smallest on the same copy; record size per preset; Lossless skips AVIF and HEIC?
6. Toggle location, camera, comments, copyright separately; inspect one output's metadata.
7. Drop a folder; drop on the Dock icon.
8. Inspector shows split, before, after, difference?
9. Animated GIF and WebP stay animated?
10. KB or MB limit: result fits, or app says it cannot?
11. Any macOS permission prompt? (Page says none.)
12. Settings switch to turn off update checks?
B. Preview, on your macOS
1. Open With, Preview; Tools, Adjust Size; note exact labels (Resample image, Resolution, estimated size).
2. Resize a copy and compare file size; confirm the steps actually shrink it.
3. File, Export: Quality slider for JPEG present and effective?
4. Several images in one window: Adjust Size applies to all selected?
C. Decision rules
- A step that differs from the page: rewrite that guide line to what you saw.
- Core promise fails (output not smaller, or originals choice not honoured): stop.
